questions.q: The page number and word count of the open document are shown on the —
questions.solution: The **status bar** at the bottom shows Page x of y, the live word count, language and the zoom slider.

questions.q: A full mesh of 8 computers needs how many links?
questions.solution: 8x7/2 = **28**. 56 skips the halving; 64 is 8 squared.

questions.q: To select the **entire worksheet** at once, press —
questions.solution: **Ctrl+A** selects all; one press covers the sheet (a second press extends it in older versions).

questions.q: The total number of cells in one Excel 2016 worksheet is —
questions.solution: 16,384 columns multiplied by 1,048,576 rows = **17,179,869,184 cells** (about 17.18 billion).

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

They said, "Hurrah! We have won the trophy."
options: They said with joy that they have won the trophy.
They exclaimed with joy that they would win the trophy.
They exclaimed with joy that they had won the trophy.
They exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the trophy.
questions.solution: Hurrah → **exclaimed with joy**; present perfect → past perfect; we → they. B inverts the tone; C keeps the un-shifted 'have won'; D changes the tense to would.
questions.shortcut: Hurrah = joy, Alas = sorrow; then backshift the tense.

questions.q: The tone of the passage is:
questions.solution: The passage only explains three scientific reasons and one exception. There are no jokes, no faults pointed out and no fond memories of the past — it simply informs.
questions.shortcut: Facts + explanation + no evaluative words = informative/neutral.
questions.passage: Honey does not spoil easily because of three properties. It contains very little water, so the microbes that cause decay cannot grow in it. It is slightly acidic. And bees add an enzyme that slowly produces small amounts of hydrogen peroxide, a substance that kills germs. If honey is left open to damp air, however, it can absorb moisture and begin to ferment.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To turn the tables
options: to cheat in a game of cards
to reverse a situation and gain the upper hand over an opponent
questions.solution: *Turn the tables* = to change a losing position into a winning one against someone. 'Lose badly' is the opposite; furniture is literal.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  The manager was angry ___ the delay in delivery.
questions.solution: **Angry at** a thing or situation; angry **with** a person. The delay is a thing → at.

questions.q: Silent Valley National Park, famous for the lion-tailed macaque, is in which state?
questions.solution: **Silent Valley** (Palakkad district, Kerala) preserves a rare stretch of untouched rainforest and the endangered **lion-tailed macaque**. Eravikulam (Nilgiri tahr) is also in Kerala.

questions.q: Day and night on the Earth are caused by:
questions.solution: The Earth's **rotation** on its axis once in about 24 hours turns one half towards the Sun (day) and the other away (night). Revolution causes the seasons.

questions.q: Which was the first national park of India?
questions.solution: **Jim Corbett NP** (Uttarakhand), established in **1936** as Hailey National Park, is India's first national park and the first Project Tiger reserve (1973).

questions.q: Which continent is **completely covered** in the statements: (1) no permanent population, (2) about 98% under an ice sheet?
questions.solution: **Antarctica** - scientists stay temporarily at research stations (India: Dakshin Gangotri, Maitri, Bharati); it is the coldest continent (Vostok, about -89 C).

questions.q: A man rides to his office at 40 km/h and returns by the same route at 60 km/h. His average speed for the round trip is:
questions.solution: $\bar{S} = \frac{2 \times 40 \times 60}{100} = 48$ km/h.

questions.q: Express $3.1\overline{45}$ as a fraction.
questions.solution:
Whole part 3. Decimal part $0.1\overline{45}$: numerator $= 145 - 1 = 144$, denominator $= 990$ (two 9s for '45', one 0 for '1').
$\frac{144}{990} = \frac{8}{55}$. So $3.1\overline{45} = 3 + \frac{8}{55} = \frac{173}{55}$.

questions.q: A shopkeeper sells article A at 20% profit and article B at 10% profit. If the overall profit is 14%, the ratio of the cost prices of A and B is:
questions.shortcut: A's profit sits above the mean, so its arm is the smaller one.

questions.q: $\frac{3}{5}$ of a number is 63 more than $\frac{1}{4}$ of the number. What is the number?
questions.solution: $\left(\frac{3}{5} - \frac{1}{4}\right)x = 63 \Rightarrow \frac{7}{20}x = 63 \Rightarrow x = 180$.

questions.q: If **dog is called cat**, **cat is called rat**, **rat is called lion**, and **lion is called cow**, which animal catches mice?
questions.solution: A real **cat** catches mice. Cat is called **rat**. Answer: Rat. (Cat is only the new name of a dog.)

questions.q:
**Statements:** All shirts are cotton.

**Conclusions:**
I. All shirts are white.
II. Some shirts are not white.

Which of the conclusions follow(s)?
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution: Nothing links shirts with white, so neither follows alone; the pair is a true negation pair. **Either I or II follows.**
questions.shortcut: The statements may ignore the pair completely — the pair rule still works.

questions.q: In a certain code, **HIDE is written as SRWV**. How is **GOAT** written in that code?
questions.solution: H(8)+S(19) = 27, I(9)+R(18) = 27 — **opposite letters**. G↔T, O↔L, A↔Z, T↔G → **TLZG**.
questions.shortcut: 27-sum check, then the opposite-pairs table does the whole question.

questions.q: In a code language, **'blue sky' is written 'ta pa'** and **'sky walk' is written 'pa sa'**. What is the code for **'blue'**?
questions.solution: 'sky' is common to both sentences and 'pa' is the common code → sky = pa. In sentence 1 the leftover word 'blue' takes the leftover code **ta**.
questions.shortcut: Common word ↔ common code; leftovers pair up.
